_comment: WHY THIS EXISTS: the custom role grants Microsoft.ContainerRegistry/*,
which includes registries/write. ACR bills a flat daily rate per
registry by tier, so the SKU is the whole cost decision - Premium is a
large step up from Standard and buys capabilities (geo-replication,
higher throughput, private link) an innovation sandbox does not need.
WHY A CUSTOM DEFINITION: the only SKU-touching built-in for ACR is
SKUs that support Private Links'. Verified 2026-09-25 - that policy
pushes registries UP to Premium, because Premium is the tier that
supports private link. It is the exact OPPOSITE of a cost ceiling and
That tension is real and worth stating: if this workload later requires
private link on its registry, Premium becomes a requirement and the two
controls genuinely conflict. Resolve it by adding Premium to
ACR_ALLOWED_SKUS deliberately, with the cost accepted - not by removing
ALIAS VERIFIED against the live provider:

properties.displayName: Container registries must use an approved SKU
properties.description: Denies or audits Microsoft.ContainerRegistry registries created with a SKU outside the approved list. ACR bills a flat daily rate per registry by tier, so the SKU is the cost decision. Premium is excluded by default.

metadata.description: Audit reports without blocking. Deny blocks the deployment.
Permitted sku.name values for Microsoft.ContainerRegistry/registries. Premium is deliberately excluded as the cost tier; add it only with the spend accepted.
